nahhas-irab:1-1.t: المر تِلْكَ آياتُ الْكِتابِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The implied form may also be: "This which has been sent down to you — those are the verses of the Book that you were promised". وَالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ الْحَقُّ: mubtadaʾ and khabar. الذي may also be conjoined to آيات, in the position of the nominative, with الحق nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of الذي, or on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ. الذي may also be in the position of the genitive, conjoined to الكتاب, with الحق nominative on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ; and it may be genitive as a naʿt of الذي. وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ: that is, after the signs have become clear.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: اللَّهُ الَّذِي رَفَعَ السَّماواتِ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. they must have someone who raises them, and this is one of the signs. بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَها: «ترونها» may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. He raised the heavens, visible, without pillars. It may also be resumptive, i.e. He raised the heavens without pillars, then said: you see them. And تَرَوْنَها may be in the position of the genitive, i.e. without visible pillars — that is, had they been on pillars you would have seen them, because of the thickness of the pillars.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَدَّ الْأَرْضَ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); so He pointed to His power, Mighty and Majestic, in the earth after pointing to it in the heaven. وَجَعَلَ فِيها رَواسِيَ: the yāʾ was given a vowel in the accusative position because of the lightness of the fatḥa, and it is a diptote because it has come to be treated like the sound [noun]. أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ [Luqmān: 10] is in the position of the accusative, i.e. out of aversion that it should sway with you.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: وَفِي الْأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُتَجاوِراتٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and by this He pointed to His power, Mighty and Majestic. وَجَنَّاتٌ مِنْ أَعْنابٍ: conjoined. «وجنات» [in the accusative] is also permissible, on [the implication of] «وجعل فيها جنات»; and it may be in the position of the genitive, conjoined to كلّ. وَزَرْعٌ وَنَخِيلٌ صِنْوانٌ وَغَيْرُ صِنْوانٍ: with the genitive, the reading of the people of Medina and the people of Kufa; Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read (وزرع) in the nominative, and what follows likewise. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: I said to Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ: "Why do you not read «وزرع» in the genitive?" He said: "Gardens are not made of crops." Abū Jaʿfar said: what Abū ʿAmr, may Allah have mercy on him, said does not bind those who read the genitive, because after it the palms are mentioned, and when crops are combined with palms, both together are called a garden (janna). It is reported that Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said that «وزرع ونخيل» in the genitive is preferable because it is closer to it, and he cited Sībawayh's report: خشّنت بصدره وصدر زيد, where the genitive is preferable to the accusative because of its proximity to it; likewise «وزرع» is preferable because of its proximity to أعناب. «صنوان» is the plural of صنو, like نسوة / نسوان and قنو / قنوان; Sībawayh reported قنوان. Al-Farrāʾ said: «صنوان» with ḍamma is the dialect of Tamīm and Qays, and with kasra the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. If you form the plural of صنو for a small number you say أصناء, and for a large number صنيّ and صنيّ [Translator's note: the two forms are presumably distinguished by vowelling (ṣuniyy / ṣiniyy), not shown in the source]. Al-Ḥasan, ʿĀṣim, Ḥumayd and Ibn Muḥayṣin read يُسْقى with yāʾ, treating النبت (the plants) or the collective as masculine. Abū ʿAmr argued for the feminine on the grounds that after it comes وَنُفَضِّلُ بَعْضَها, and He did not say بعضه. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a good argument. The people of the two Sanctuaries and the people of Basra read وَنُفَضِّلُ with nūn, and the people of Kufa except ʿĀṣim read ويفضّل with yāʾ. Abū ʿUbayd said: ونفضّل is resumptive, and ويفضّل refers back to the beginning of the sura. [It was objected that] this is something that has come earlier and been separated off by His words, Mighty and Majestic: وَفِي الْأَرْضِ قِطَعٌ مُتَجاوِراتٌ [al-Raʿd: 4]. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a good argument. إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ: [يَعْقِلُونَ is] in the position of the genitive, i.e. people of understanding.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
وَإِنْ تَعْجَبْ فَعَجَبٌ قَوْلُهُمْ: that is, people of understanding ought to marvel at their saying, because it is ignorance, since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had pointed them to His power and shown them of His signs what is greater than the reviving of the dead.
«عجب» is nominative, with postponement intended, as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject). أَإِذا كُنَّا تُراباً: what governs «إذا» is كنا, because what comes after إنّ may not govern what precedes it. If one reads «أإنّا», then what governs «إذا» is an omitted verb, the implied form being "Shall we be resurrected when…". أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ: that is, whoever asks about the resurrection as one who denies it, after the proofs, has disbelieved. Comparable to this is ما يُجادِلُ فِي آياتِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا [Ghāfir: 4], i.e. the disputing of one who denies. وَأُولئِكَ: mubtadaʾ. (والأغلال): a second mubtadaʾ. فِي أَعْناقِهِمْ: in the position of the khabar, and the clause is the khabar of the first. وَأُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ: mubtadaʾ and khabar.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
وَيَسْتَعْجِلُونَكَ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ قَبْلَ الْحَسَنَةِ: Qatāda said: [they hasten] punishment before well-being. Abū Isḥāq said:
It is from their saying: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain stones upon us from the sky or bring us a painful punishment." وَقَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمُ الْمَثُلاتُ: we have mentioned what there is on it. Al-Farrāʾ said: the Banū Tamīm say مثلات with a quiescent thāʾ. وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ لِلنَّاسِ عَلى ظُلْمِهِمْ: it is related that Ibn ʿAbbās said: there is nothing in the Qur'an more hope-inspiring than this.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ: they said this only after the signs and proofs had appeared, out of obstinacy and mockery, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: إِنَّما أَنْتَ مُنْذِرٌ, i.e. you warn them of the punishment for their disbelief after the proofs. وَلِكُلِّ قَوْمٍ هادٍ: we have mentioned the view of the exegetes on it. There are two construals in Arabic grammar: هاد may be conjoined to منذر — and this is among the best things said about it, because the warner is the one who guides to Allah, Mighty and Majestic — the implied form being "You are only a warner, a guide". The other construal is that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being "and for every people there is a guiding prophet".

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ أُنْثى: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and likewise وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ بِمِقْدارٍ.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: عالِمُ الْغَيْبِ: a naʿt (adjective); or, if you wish, on the implication of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); or, if you wish, as a mubtadaʾ with what follows as its khabar (predicate). In grammar the accusative as praise and the genitive as badal (substitute) are also permissible. الْكَبِيرُ: the King who has power over every thing. الْمُتَعالِ: the One exalted above every thing; the yāʾ was dropped because it is the end of a verse.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
سَواءٌ مِنْكُمْ: nominative, with postponement intended. Abū Isḥāq said: the implied form is "possessing equality", as one says رجل عدل (a just man, lit. "a man of justice"). It is said: سواء means مستو (equal), and it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). Abū Isḥāq said:
According to Sībawayh this is not permissible, because one does not begin with an indefinite noun. Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is that these are equal before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His knowledge of them is one. Ḥassān said: [al-Wāfir] 243-
فمن يهجو رسول الله منكم ... ويمدحه وينصره سواء
(Whoever of you satirises the Messenger of Allah, or praises him and supports him, it is all the same.)
That is, in his standing before Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: لَهُ مُعَقِّباتٌ: the plural of معقّبة, the hāʾ being for intensiveness; that is why يَحْفَظُونَهُ is permissible in the masculine. مِنْ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ: that is, their guarding him is by Allah's command — Mighty and Majestic — He commanded them to guard him against what has not been decreed. It is said: the meaning is that the مُعَقِّبات are from Allah's command, Mighty and Majestic. These two answers are according to those who say the مُعَقِّبات are the angels. As for those who say the مُعَقِّبات are the guards (shuraṭ), the meaning for them is: they guard him from Allah's command, according to their claim. إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُغَيِّرُ ما بِقَوْمٍ حَتَّى يُغَيِّرُوا ما بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ: there are two views on it. One is that the meaning is: Allah does not change the favour and honour He began with a person by punishing or tormenting him, unless he changes what is in himself. The other view: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not change the condition of a righteous believing people, calling them disbelievers and transgressors, unless they do what necessitates that, and He does not command their humiliation unless they change what is in themselves. وَإِذا أَرادَ اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ سُوْءاً فَلا مَرَدَّ لَهُ: so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, warned them after informing them that He knows their secrets and what they conceal. وَما لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ والٍ: that is, no protector to help them and defend them.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: هُوَ الَّذِي يُرِيكُمُ الْبَرْقَ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). خَوْفاً وَطَمَعاً: as maṣdars (verbal nouns). The exegetes say: fear for the traveller and hope for the resident, for the most part; in reality it applies generally to everyone who fears or hopes. وَيُنْشِئُ السَّحابَ الثِّقالَ: [السحاب is] the plural of سحابة, and that is why it is described with الثقال.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: وَيُسَبِّحُ الرَّعْدُ بِحَمْدِهِ: the exegetes say: الرعد is the name of an angel, so this is literal. It is also said that it is figurative and that it is the sound; then the meaning of يسبح is that it indicates Allah's transcendence, Mighty and Majestic, above all likenesses, and so glorification is attributed to it figuratively.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: وَما دُعاءُ الْكافِرِينَ: that is, the disbelievers' calling upon idols. إِلَّا فِي ضَلالٍ: away from what is right and from benefiting by an answer.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: the scholars have discussed the meaning of this, and among the best things said is that prostration here is submission to Allah's ordering, Mighty and Majestic, and His disposal [of them], in health, sickness and other things.
طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً: that is, they are led along whether they like it or dislike it; they have no stratagem in that. Their shadows too are subject to Allah's ordering, Mighty and Majestic, and His making the sun run, with the shadow's increase and decrease and its disappearing through the passing of time and the course of the sun, as He, Mighty and Majestic, has ordained.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمى وَالْبَصِيرُ: that is, the believer and the disbeliever. أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي الظُّلُماتُ وَالنُّورُ: that is, disbelief and faith.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t:
فَسالَتْ أَوْدِيَةٌ بِقَدَرِها: the exegetes said: i.e. according to the measure of what fills them; and it is said: what was decreed for them.
فَاحْتَمَلَ السَّيْلُ زَبَداً رابِياً: the sentence ends here. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيْهِ فِي النَّارِ ابْتِغاءَ حِلْيَةٍ أَوْ مَتاعٍ زَبَدٌ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) according to the Basrans. Al-Kisāʾī said: it is nominative because its meaning is "from what you kindle in the fire there is froth". He said: and it is الغثاء (scum); غثى يغثي غثيا وغثيانا; it is what is of no benefit. مثله: that is, like the froth of the sea. كَذلِكَ: in the position of the accusative. فَأَمَّا الزَّبَدُ: that is, from these things. فَيَذْهَبُ جُفاءً: as a ḥāl (circumstantial); from their saying انجفأت القدر, when the pot throws off its froth; it too is الغثاء.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: لِلَّذِينَ اسْتَجابُوا لِرَبِّهِمُ الْحُسْنى: [الحسنى is] in the position of the nominative; the implied form may be "the reward of the best", and it is said: it is a name for Paradise. أولئك لهم سوء الحساب: the scrutiny, the rebuke, and the cancelling of good deeds by bad deeds.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: الَّذِينَ يُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ: in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from His words, Mighty and Majestic: إِنَّما يَتَذَكَّرُ أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: كَذلِكَ أَرْسَلْناكَ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative. الأمة is the community.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: وَالَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ ما أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَنْ يُوصَلَ: that is, they maintain their ties of kinship, and [ties with] those of the people of obedience whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded to be honoured and revered.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: وَيَدْرَؤُنَ بِالْحَسَنَةِ السَّيِّئَةَ: that is, they repel; when they are inclined to an evil deed, they reflect, restrain themselves, and repel it by seeking forgiveness and desisting. This is a good deed. They also forbid wrongdoing, by admonition or by harshness, and all of this is good. أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عُقْبَى الدَّارِ.

nahhas-irab:23-24.t:
جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ: a badal (substitute) from عقبى. يَدْخُلُونَها وَمَنْ صَلَحَ: this is one of the difficult points of grammar, because most grammarians say: ضربته وزيد ("I struck him, and Zayd") is ugly until the latent/attached pronoun is reinforced. The grammarians discussed this, until a group of them said: قمت وزيد is good with an alif [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense of "with an alif" is unclear], because this is not like the genitive, since the genitive pronoun is never separated. Abū Isḥāq held that the better form is قمت وزيدا, meaning "together", unless the speech is lengthened, so that you say: قمت في الدار وزيد, and ضربتك أمس وزيد — and if you wish, you use the accusative. In this, regard is paid only to what is separated, which is treated like reinforcement (tawkīd). Abū Jaʿfar said: in my view — and Allah knows best — «من» may be in the position of the nominative, the implied form being: "Those, and whoever is righteous among their fathers, spouses and offspring, theirs is the final abode."
وَالْمَلائِكَةُ: mubtadaʾ (subject). يَدْخُلُونَ: in the position of the khabar (predicate), and the implied form is: [they enter] saying: سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ: this too was out of obstinacy, after they had seen the signs.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from (من). وَتَطْمَئِنُّ قُلُوبُهُمْ بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ: that is, by His promise. أَلا: [a particle of] alerting. بِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ: that is, their hearts.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is طُوبى لَهُمْ. الَّذِينَ may also be in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from «من», or meaning "I mean". And طُوبى may be in the position of the accusative, meaning "Allah has granted them ṭūbā".

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ الْجِبالُ: «أنّ» is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "if this occurred". The scholars have several views on this verse. One is that the apodosis is omitted, the implied form being "it would have been this Qur'an"; and it is said the implied form is "they would not have believed". Al-Kisāʾī said: the meaning is "We wished that there were a Qur'an by which the mountains were moved", and so this is without omission. Al-Farrāʾ has a good view on it. He said: the apodosis is in what precedes it, i.e. "and they disbelieve in the Most Merciful, even if there were a Qur'an by which the mountains were moved". بَلْ لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ جَمِيعاً: [جَمِيعاً] as a ḥāl (circumstantial). أَفَلَمْ يَيْأَسِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: there are several dialect forms in it: one says يائس, and one says ييئس on the pattern فعل يفعل, and one says يئس يئس, the imperfect having the same form as the past [Translator's note: the forms are distinguished only by vowelling, which the source does not show]. أَنْ لَوْ يَشاءُ اللَّهُ: in the position of the accusative.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قائِمٌ عَلى كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, indicated by وَجَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكاءَ. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said: the implied form is "like their partners". قُلْ سَمُّوهُمْ: that is, name them by a creation they created or a deed they did by their own power. أَمْ بِظاهِرٍ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ: it is said its meaning is: it has no reality; and it is said: or by an apparent statement mentioned in the scriptures. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read وَصُدُّوا with kasra on the ṣād, because the original is صددوا, and the vowel of the dāl was shifted onto the ṣād.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
لَهُمْ عَذابٌ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا:
Allah's cursing them, Mighty and Majestic, and the believers' hostility towards them.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
مَثَلُ الْجَنَّةِ الَّتِي وُعِدَ الْمُتَّقُونَ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) according to Sībawayh; the implied form for him is: "In what is related to you is the likeness of the Garden", or "The likeness of the Garden is in what We relate to you". Al-Farrāʾ said: what makes it nominative is تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ, the meaning being "the Garden that the God-fearing were promised, rivers flow beneath it", as one says: حلية فلان أسمر ("so-and-so's description: dark"). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: whoever says مثل means صفة (description) has erred, because one says only:
صفة فلان أنه ظريف وأنه كريم ("so-and-so's description is that he is witty and generous"), and one says: مثل زيد مثل عمرو ("Zayd's likeness is ʿAmr's likeness"). «مثل» is taken from المثال (pattern) and الحذو (model), while صفة is taken from التحلية (portraying) and النعت (describing). The implied form is only: "In what is related to you is the likeness of the Garden." أُكُلُها دائِمٌ: and in it is such-and-such, and in it is such-and-such. تِلْكَ عُقْبَى الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا: mubtadaʾ and khabar (predicate), and likewise وَعُقْبَى الْكافِرِينَ النَّارُ.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: وَالَّذِينَ آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ: it is said He means by it the believers, and the Book is the Qur'an. وَمِنَ الْأَحْزابِ: that is, those who banded together in enmity to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and the believers reject what did not agree with them. It is also said: those given the Book are the Jews and the Christians, who rejoice at the Qur'an because it confirms their prophets and their scriptures, even if they did not believe in Muḥammad ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:38-39.t: وَما كانَ لِرَسُولٍ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِآيَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ: that is, except by His permitting him to ask for the sign, so that he knows there is benefit in that. لِكُلِّ أَجَلٍ كِتابٌ: that is, for every nation there is a written decree and a determined, decided matter which the angels come to know, so that Allah's power, Mighty and Majestic, is known thereby; and likewise وَعِنْدَهُ أُمُّ الْكِتابِ. We have already explained the meaning of يَمْحُوا اللَّهُ ما يَشاءُ وَيُثْبِتُ.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: وَإِنْ ما نُرِيَنَّكَ: in the position of the jussive by the condition, and the nūn entered for emphasis.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
نَنْقُصُها مِنْ أَطْرافِها: the plural of طرف. We have mentioned the view of the exegetes on it. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: الطرف is the noble part of everything, and its plural is أطراف, as al-Aʿshā said: [al-Ṭawīl] 244-
هم الطّرف النّاكي العدوّ وأنتم ... بقصوى ثلاث تأكلون الوقائصا ]
(They are the noble ones who wound the enemy, while you, at the farthest of three [stages], eat the broken-necked beasts.)
He said: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: «Knowledge is valleys; in whichever valley you take of it, you will be exhausted, so take from everything a ṭaraf» — i.e. the choicest. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said نَنْقُصُها مِنْ أَطْرافِها, i.e. by [taking] its scholars, and the scholars are the choicest, the noble. From this is «He does not know which of his two ṭarafs is longer», i.e. he does not know, because of his simple-mindedness, whether nobility comes to him from his father's side or his mother's side. الطّرف is also the noble horse, and الطّارف is newly acquired property.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: فَلِلَّهِ الْمَكْرُ جَمِيعاً: that is, to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, belongs the abiding plotting that encompasses its people. The meaning of plotting on the part of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is that He sends down punishment upon whoever deserves it from where he does not know. وَسَيَعْلَمُ الْكُفَّارُ: and الكافر [in the other reading] has the same meaning, a singular standing for a plural.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: قُلْ كَفى بِاللَّهِ: [الله is] in the position of the nominative. شَهِيداً: as a specification (bayān). وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ: in the position of the genitive, conjoined according to the wording; it may also be in the position of the nominative according to the meaning. عِلْمُ الْكِتابِ: nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
